why_not_served_from_it: tests/security/check is writable only by W17-01 and W17-02 (plan write_scope), and it is accepted card W17-01's deliverable; editing it from a W09 card would rewrite an accepted card
the program emits host-boundary ids (BOOT/CRED/IPC/WS/REVOKE/EXPIRY) with no check-id routing, so it has no way to answer for W0902-* rows
appending W09-02 to the key without that routing would answer a W09 dispatch with W17's roster, which is a fabricated PASS and the one outcome the registry append rule exists to stop

legacy_map.note: routes W09 through the gate id W09-G02 and cases A06/C02/C22, never through the card id W09-02; v2.4 resolution prefers execution/v2.4/commands.json

asks_reviewer_to_judge: Is serving a card's rows from a new key, when the plan named another card's key whose handler is uneditable and mis-routed, an acceptable increment or a plan defect that should block acceptance instead?
